dev_mode_suffix: Dev-mode note: this run targets the SolvaPay dev backend (api-dev.solvapay.com). Pass `--dev` to every published-CLI invocation (`npm create solvapay@latest ... --dev`) and to the agent-path scaffolder (`node scripts/scaffold.mjs ... --dev`); both seed `SOLVAPAY_API_BASE_URL=https://api-dev.solvapay.com` into the project `.env`. When no scaffolder runs (the prompt fixes `.env` contents, or the task is to hand-write a server), set `SOLVAPAY_API_BASE_URL=https://api-dev.solvapay.com` yourself — append the line to any `.env` the setup block created, and read the var via `env.SOLVAPAY_API_BASE_URL` / `process.env.SOLVAPAY_API_BASE_URL` in code.

evals.prompt: Context: run scaffolder scripts via `<skills-repo>/skills/create-mcp-app/scripts/describe.mjs` and `scaffold.mjs` (set SCAFFOLDER_SCRIPTS_DIR or npm install create-solvapay if resolution fails). Task: Generate an MCP server from `https://petstore.swagger.io/v2/swagger.json` into `./petstore-mcp`. Use intent-driven mode.
evals.expected_output: A scaffolded Cloudflare Workers MCP project at ./petstore-mcp/ with src/tools/ containing true intent-driven clusters (action-verb names like manage_pet, find_pet — NOT tag-named files like pets.ts/users.ts). selections.json written outside the project. Tools follow references/tool-design.md response-mode contract (c.respond with text narration). Tier assignments respect describe.mjs's suggestedTier output.
expectations: src/tools/ contains action-verb intent files (manage_pet.ts, find_pet.ts, manage_order.ts, manage_user.ts or similar) — NOT tag-grouped files like pets.ts/users.ts/store.ts, and NOT one-file-per-operation (no addPet.ts, getPetById.ts, deletePet.ts, etc.)
Paid tools (ctx.registerPayable) use c.respond(data, { text: narration }) — NOT raw return { content: [...] } from paid handlers

Free tools (ctx.server.registerTool) return { content: [{ type: 'text', text: <render-instruction narration> }], structuredContent: {...} } — they include a text narration alongside structuredContent, not raw content with no narration
Free vs paid tier assignment in tool files matches describe.mjs's suggestedTier output — GET/read operations registered with ctx.server.registerTool, mutations registered with ctx.registerPayable
selections.json is NOT found anywhere inside ./petstore-mcp/ (security requirement — upstream API key would leak)
The agent ran node scripts/describe.mjs against the spec (visible in transcript)
The agent ran node scripts/scaffold.mjs to generate the project (visible in transcript)

The agent read references/from-openapi/guide.md, references/tool-design.md, AND references/from-openapi/intent-driven.md before authoring tools (visible in transcript) — intent-driven.md is load-bearing for clustering patterns

scaffold.mjs succeeded on the first invocation (no 'target dir exists' error in transcript; agent did not have to retry)
src/tools/ contains one file per non-skipped Petstore v3 operation (one-to-one mode — many files like getPetById.ts, findPetsByStatus.ts, etc.)
src/tools/index.ts exists with a registerTools aggregator that imports and calls each per-operation register function
The agent ran node scripts/describe.mjs against the local temp spec file

The tool's handler returns c.respond(data, { text: narration }) — NOT raw content arrays, NOT custom MCP response shapes, NOT iframes/UI payloads
./petstore-mcp/src/tools/index.ts was updated to import and call the new tool's register function
The original ./petstore-mcp/package.json, wrangler.jsonc, and src/worker.ts were NOT overwritten or deleted
The agent read references/tool-design.md before authoring the tool (visible in transcript)

The agent read references/hosting/cloudflare/ or references/from-openapi/deploy.md (visible in transcript)
The agent mentioned wrangler whoami or a workers.dev subdomain pre-flight check

The agent identified the correct env var split: SOLVAPAY_SECRET_KEY is a Worker secret (uploaded once via npx wrangler secret put, never in wrangler.jsonc and never as a --var flag); SOLVAPAY_PRODUCT_REF and MCP_PUBLIC_BASE_URL live in wrangler.jsonc [vars] as placeholders/defaults AND get overridden at deploy time via --var flags from scripts/deploy.mjs sourcing .env

evals.prompt: Context: run scaffolder scripts via `<skills-repo>/skills/create-mcp-app/scripts/describe.mjs` and `scaffold.mjs`. Task: Generate an MCP server from `https://petstore.swagger.io/v2/swagger.json` into `./petstore-mcp-gated`. Use intent-driven mode at the default (standard) confirmation level, then author the intent-tool files matching the cluster proposal you surfaced at G2.
evals.expected_output: The agent surfaces gate G2 — a structured cluster proposal listing the proposed intent_name / ops covered / tier / one-line description rows — BEFORE writing selections.json or invoking scaffold.mjs. After G2 approval, the agent surfaces gate G6 (selections.json preview with upstreamAuth.key redacted, showing the resolved mode / workerName / upstreamAuth payload) before running scaffold.mjs. After scaffold, the agent authors one `src/tools/<intent>.ts` per row of the G2 proposal and wires the aggregator. Gates use stable id strings (G2:approve, G6:run).
expectations: The agent presented a cluster proposal (gate G2) BEFORE authoring any src/tools/*.ts file or invoking scaffold.mjs — the proposal lists at least intent_name + ops covered + tier per row
The G2 proposal labels the gate explicitly (e.g. 'G2', 'Gate G2', or includes the canonical option ids approve / edit / oneToOne) so eval transcripts can grep for it
The agent waited for user approval on G2 before writing selections.json — did NOT skip straight from describe.mjs output to scaffold.mjs in one turn

The agent surfaced gate G6 (selections.json preview) before invoking scaffold.mjs — the preview redacts upstreamAuth.key as '<redacted>' (or equivalent) and shows the resolved mode / workerName / upstreamAuth payload (note: in intent-driven mode there is no operations[] field — that exists only in one-to-one mode)
selections.json is NOT found anywhere inside ./petstore-mcp-gated/ (the secret-key redaction in G6 is render-time only; the file written to /tmp still contains the real key)
The agent read references/from-openapi/intent-driven.md and references/from-openapi/scaffold.md (visible in transcript) — both define the gates this eval asserts
src/tools/ contains intent-driven action-verb files (manage_pet.ts, find_pet.ts, etc.) after scaffold + authoring, matching the cluster proposal surfaced at G2

evals.prompt: Task: Scaffold a brand-new paid MCP server (no OpenAPI input) into `./haiku-mcp`. I want a single paid tool called `generate_haiku` that takes a `topic` string and an optional `mood` enum ('serene' | 'melancholy' | 'playful'), and returns a 3-line haiku as `{ lines: string[3] }`. Replace the scaffolder's placeholder tool — don't leave it dangling.
evals.expected_output: A fresh Cloudflare Workers project at `./haiku-mcp/` produced from the from-scratch (no-OpenAPI) scaffold flow. Exactly one paid tool, `generate_haiku`, lives in its own `src/tools/generate_haiku.ts` exporting `registerGenerateHaiku(ctx)`. The placeholder tool from the scaffold is gone — neither its file nor its register-call survives. `src/tools/index.ts` imports + calls `registerGenerateHaiku`. Handler uses `c.respond(data, { text })` narration. Schema validates `topic: z.string()` and `mood: z.enum(['serene','melancholy','playful']).optional()`. No OpenAPI scripts (describe.mjs / scaffold.mjs from `scripts/mcp/`) were invoked — those are the spec-first agent path.
expectations: The agent ran `npm create solvapay` with `--type mcp --no-openapi` (or `pnpm/yarn create solvapay --no-openapi`) — not describe.mjs/scaffold.mjs from the OpenAPI agent path
The project is rooted at `./haiku-mcp/` with `package.json`, `wrangler.jsonc`, and `src/worker.ts` calling `createSolvaPayMcpFetch` (or equivalent fetch-first factory)
`src/tools/generate_haiku.ts` exists and exports `registerGenerateHaiku(ctx, env?)` (per the file-layout convention)

The scaffolder's placeholder tool (e.g. `helloTool`/`placeholder`/`hello`) is no longer registered — its file is deleted or replaced, and `src/tools/index.ts` does NOT import/call any leftover placeholder register function
`generate_haiku` is registered via `ctx.registerPayable('generate_haiku', { title, description, schema, handler, annotations? })` — the 2-arg shape, second arg a single config object
The handler returns `c.respond({ lines: [...] }, { text: <narration with render instruction> })` — not raw content arrays, not iframe payloads
The Zod schema validates `topic: z.string()` (required) and `mood: z.enum(['serene','melancholy','playful']).optional()`

The agent read `references/from-scratch/guide.md` AND `references/from-scratch/scaffold-and-extend.md` AND `references/tool-design.md` (visible in transcript) — all three are load-bearing for the placeholder-replacement workflow

evals.prompt: Task: I want to set up a paid MCP server, but I'm running on Node + Express (NOT Cloudflare Workers) — my company doesn't use Cloudflare. Walk me through how to wire SolvaPay into an Express app from scratch: which package subpath, which factory, how to mount the OAuth bridge, how to wrap a paid tool. I'll write the actual `app.listen` glue myself; you produce a minimal `server.ts` (Express handler + SolvaPay factory + one example paid tool) that compiles and a `package.json` listing the right deps. Save everything under `./express-mcp/`.
evals.expected_output: A Node + Express MCP server at `./express-mcp/` using `createSolvaPayMcpServer` from `@solvapay/mcp` wired to `StreamableHTTPServerTransport`, with `createMcpOAuthBridge` from `@solvapay/mcp/express` mounted as middleware. Env vars via `process.env`. No `wrangler.jsonc`. One paid tool with correct `registerPayable` 2-arg shape and `c.respond` handler.
expectations: `./express-mcp/server.ts` imports `createSolvaPayMcpServer` from `@solvapay/mcp` AND `createMcpOAuthBridge` from `@solvapay/mcp/express` — NOT `createSolvaPayMcpFetch` from `@solvapay/mcp/fetch` and NOT a nonexistent `createSolvaPayMcpExpress`
`./express-mcp/server.ts` uses `StreamableHTTPServerTransport` from `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` to bridge the MCP server to Express (req, res)
`./express-mcp/package.json` declares `@solvapay/mcp`, `@solvapay/server`, `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`, and `express` as dependencies
Env vars are read via `process.env.SOLVAPAY_SECRET_KEY` etc. — NOT a Workers `Env` interface and NOT `env.SOLVAPAY_SECRET_KEY` from a Workers fetch signature
No `wrangler.jsonc` is created (Cloudflare-specific; not applicable on Express)
At least one paid tool is registered via `ctx.registerPayable(name, { title, description, schema, handler })` with the 2-arg shape, and its handler returns `c.respond(data, { text })`
The agent did NOT run the OpenAPI agent path (`describe.mjs` / `scaffold.mjs` from `scripts/mcp/`) — there is no OpenAPI spec in this task
The agent read references/hosting/alternatives.md (visible in transcript) — it is the routing doc that documents the Node + Express wiring pattern
